selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now inventory-api succeeded; systemctl is-active returned 'active'; curl to /health and /inventory returned valid JSON; oom_score_adj confirmed as -1000 for the running PID
Captured node memory profile (2GB RAM, no swap, cgroup v2) and confirmed inventory-api active and serving /health prior to starting the memory hog

selected_evidence.requirement: Memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory
selected_evidence.summary: mem-hog.service started and progressively consumed memory (free -h showing used climbing from ~380Mi to 1.9Gi/1.9Gi total, i.e. full exhaustion) while allocation log showed continuous growth to allocated_mb=1780

selected_evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
selected_evidence.summary: dmesg kernel log shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1393 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' with task_memcg=/system.slice/mem-hog.service; inventory-api's python3 (pid 1295, oom_score_adj:-1000) is listed in the same OOM report but was not killed. systemctl status confirms mem-hog.service 'Failed with result: oom-kill'

selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout and after the OOM event
selected_evidence.summary: curl http://$NODE_IP:8080/health returned status ok with continuously increasing uptime (14.5s -> 28.5s -> 41.2s -> 57.6s) across the entire disruption window, proving the process was never killed or restarted

selected_evidence.requirement: Cleanup of the disruptive test process
selected_evidence.summary: mem-hog service/script files removed, reset-failed run, memory usage back to normal baseline (~252Mi used), inventory-api confirmed still active and serving

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: pre-restart boot identity and healthy service baseline
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a; inventory-api enabled, active, and serving correct /health and /inventory data

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnection
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown so the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node went down

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proving an actual restart
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id was unchanged initially, then the node became unreachable (Connection reset by peer) during reboot, then boot_id returned as 103286eb-e943-4392-8085-28dec8a72e6b, differing from the pre-restart value

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required service and data
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot: uptime -s shows new boot time, inventory-api is enabled/active with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, /health and /inventory return correct data, mem-hog.service confirmed absent, memory usage normal

commands.command:
mkdir -p /opt/inventory-api
cat > /opt/inventory-api/app.py <<'PYEOF'
import http.server
import json
import socketserver
import time

INVENTORY = [
    {"sku": "widget-1", "qty": 42},
    {"sku": "widget-2", "qty": 17},
]
START = time.time()

class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def _json(self, obj, code=200):
        body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path == "/health":
            self._json({"status": "ok", "uptime": time.time() - START})
        elif self.path == "/inventory":
            self._json({"items": INVENTORY})
        else:
            self._json({"error": "not found"}, 404)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8080), Handler) as httpd:
        httpd.serve_forever()
PYEOF
cat /opt/inventory-api/app.py | head -3

commands.command:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory API
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/inventory-api/app.py
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
# Protect from the kernel OOM killer so it keeps serving under memory pressure
OOMScoreAdjust=-1000
OOMPolicy=continue

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now inventory-api
sleep 1
systemctl is-active inventory-api
curl -s http://$NODE_IP:8080/health
echo
curl -s http://$NODE_IP:8080/inventory
echo
cat /proc/$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value inventory-api)/oom_score_adj

cat > /opt/mem-hog.py <<'PYEOF'
import time
import sys

chunks = []
mb = 20
i = 0
while True:
    try:
        chunks.append(bytearray(mb * 1024 * 1024))
        for c in chunks:
            c[0] = 1
        i += 1
        sys.stdout.write("allocated_mb=%d\n" % (i * mb))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        time.sleep(0.3)
    except MemoryError:
        sys.stdout.write("memory_error\n")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        time.sleep(0.3)
PYEOF

[Unit]
Description=Memory hog (intentional OOM trigger for test)

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/mem-hog.py
Restart=no
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/mem-hog.log
StandardError=append:/var/log/mem-hog.log
EOF
